title: The story says Salem burned its witches. Not one of them was.
description:
Not one of them was. None of the condemned was burned at the stake. The idea likely comes from European trials, where fire was common. Salem followed English law and used the gallows.

Fourteen women and five men were hanged between 10 June and 22 September 1692.

Giles Corey was pressed to death. He was 81. He refused to enter a plea, so stones were piled on him in September 1692.

The fire belongs to Europe. Salem used rope.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salem_witch_trials: read. Established the trials running from February 1692 to May 1693; 19 executed by hanging (14 women and 5 men), the first hanging on 10 June 1692 and the last on 22 September 1692; Giles Corey, 81, pressed to death with stones over two days for refusing to plead, in September 1692; at least five others dying in jail; and that the idea of burned American witches is false.
- https://www.history.com/articles/were-witches-burned-at-the-stake-during-the-salem-witch-trials: read. Established that none of the condemned was burned at the stake, that 19 were hanged at Gallows Hill in accordance with English law, that Giles Corey was pressed to death for refusing to plead, and that the burning myth likely comes from European witch trials where fire was common.
- https://blogs.loc.gov/law/2020/10/the-crushing-death-of-giles-corey-of-salem-1692/: read (Library of Congress). Corroborated Corey as an 81 year old pressed to death between 17 and 19 September 1692 under peine forte et dure for refusing to submit to trial, and 19 people hanged.
